title: Metric-definition audit: NATQ-001 strict_recall@10 vs NATQ-002 case_hit@10 vs the frozen NATQ-002 BM25 comparator
authorizes: Inspection and this audit record only. No evaluation, no scoring, no retrieval, no inference was performed.
verdict_summary: NATQ-001 strict_recall@10 and NATQ-002 case_hit@10 differ on two independent axes: aggregation (ALL gold spans vs ANY gold span) and the span-match predicate (section_path equality required vs not required). Neither difference is a naming artefact; both are readable in the scoring code. The historical 20/40 is therefore prior evidence about a different measurement on a different dataset, not a NATQ-002 baseline.

NATQ_001_strict_recall_at_10.case_predicate: origin/grok/v2-natq-20260903:experiments/EXP-017/scripts/run_exp017.py::score_system — fully_recalled = bool(spans) and found == len(spans), where found counts spans with rank is not None and rank <= TOP_K
NATQ_001_strict_recall_at_10.match_predicate_text: version_id equality AND list(section_path) equality AND char_start < ref.char_end AND char_end > ref.char_start
NATQ_001_strict_recall_at_10.gold_schema_source: origin/grok/v2-natq-20260903:src/rag_v1/types.py::EvidenceRef (version_id, section_path, char_start, char_end) and run_eval_natq_val_001.py::load_validation, which reads e['section_path'] unconditionally

NATQ_002_case_hit_at_10.span_hit_text: a gold span is HIT at depth k if any chunk returned in the top k overlaps the span's [char_start, char_end) interval in the span's own version_id
NATQ_002_case_hit_at_10.case_hit_text: fraction of cases with at least one gold span hit in the top 10
NATQ_002_case_hit_at_10.gold_schema_evidence: evals/splits/natq-002/validation.json — every evidence object has exactly the keys char_end, char_start, quote, version_id

frozen_NATQ_002_BM25_comparator_0_375.implementation: inner next(...) over hits: h.version_id == e['version_id'] and h.char_start < e['char_end'] and h.char_end > e['char_start']; hit_at_10 = bool(hit_ranks); case_hit_at_10 = sum(hit_at_10)/n_cases
frozen_NATQ_002_BM25_comparator_0_375.note: The code and the EVAL-NATQ2-H-001 protocol text agree line for line: same document-identity + character-overlap predicate, same ANY-span aggregation, same depth 10, same per-case denominator.

all_spans_or_any_span.NATQ_001_strict_recall_at_10: ALL. A case counts only when every gold span is hit within depth 10 (score_system.fully_recalled).
all_spans_or_any_span.NATQ_002_case_hit_at_10: ANY. A case counts when at least one gold span is hit within depth 10.
all_spans_or_any_span.NATQ_002_nearest_ALL_metric: case_full_coverage@10 is NATQ-002's ALL-spans metric and is the correct aggregation analogue of strict_recall@10 — but see the predicate row; it is still not the same function.
all_spans_or_any_span.materiality: 16 of the 40 validation cases carry more than one gold span (15 with two, 1 with three), so the ANY/ALL choice is live on 40% of the partition.

what_counts_as_a_matching_passage.NATQ_001: Character-range overlap between the returned chunk and the gold span, restricted to the same version_id AND the same section_path. Not chunk identity: no gold chunk id is compared. covering_chunk_ids() is computed for diagnostics and also filters on section_path.
what_counts_as_a_matching_passage.NATQ_002: Character-range overlap within the same version_id. section_path is not compared and is not present in the gold data.
what_counts_as_a_matching_passage.consequence: A chunk whose text covers the gold span but which the chunker filed under a different section_path is a MISS under NATQ-001 and a HIT under NATQ-002. The historical runner named this class explicitly: it computes overlap_ignoring_section() to classify such misses as 'evidence-granularity' failures.
what_counts_as_a_matching_passage.neither_uses: Document identity alone is not a hit under either definition; NATQ-001 reports document_recall@10 as a separate diagnostic and NATQ-002 has no document-level metric.

multi_span_and_multi_document.NATQ_001: Each gold span is resolved independently against the ranked list; the case aggregates by AND. Cross-document cases work because each EvidenceRef carries its own version_id.
multi_span_and_multi_document.NATQ_002: Each gold span is resolved independently in that span's own version_id; the case aggregates by OR for case_hit@10 and by AND for case_full_coverage@10.
multi_span_and_multi_document.assessment: The per-span resolution rule is the same in both. Only the case-level aggregation and the predicate differ.

duplicates_ties_and_denominators.duplicate_covering_chunks: Collapsed to the best rank in both. NATQ-001 takes min(rank) over all overlapping rows (first_span_rank); NATQ-002 takes the first match in a rank-ordered list (next(...)). Equivalent — no double counting in either.
duplicates_ties_and_denominators.ties: NATQ-002 BM25 ordering is deterministic: src/rag_v1/retrieval.py orders by round(score::numeric, 9) DESC, chunk_id ASC, then numbers rank = i+1, so the returned list is rank-ordered and next(...) is min-rank. A tie can only change which chunk occupies the depth-10 boundary; it cannot change whether a span already hit above the boundary is counted.

denominators.NATQ_001_strict_recall_at_10: number of cases in the partition (40)
denominators.NATQ_002_case_hit_at_10: number of cases in the partition (40)
denominators.NATQ_002_span_recall_at_10_and_micro_MRR: number of gold spans in the partition (57 validation, 79 reserve)
denominators.note: The case-level denominators have the same shape. That similarity is what makes the two numbers look comparable, and it is the only thing about them that is.

duplicates_ties_and_denominators.unhit_spans_in_micro_MRR: contribute 0, not a dropped term (EVAL-NATQ2-H-001 metrics.primary)

separating_cases.SYN-1: multi-span, one span found — strict FAIL, case_hit PASS (aggregation)
separating_cases.SYN-6: cross-document, one document's span found — strict FAIL, case_hit PASS (aggregation)
separating_cases.SYN-2: covering chunk filed under a different section_path — strict FAIL, case_hit PASS, and full_coverage PASS (predicate; survives even after the aggregation is matched)

comparability_findings: Definition-level: NOT_EQUIVALENT. strict_recall@10 is strictly stricter than case_hit@10 on both axes, so on identical retrieval strict_recall@10 <= case_hit@10 always. The historical 20/40 = 0.50 is therefore a LOWER bound on what case_hit@10 would have been on that dataset, not an estimate of it.

Schema-level: the NATQ-001 predicate is not computable on NATQ-002 as it stands, because NATQ-002 gold evidence carries no section_path. Making the definitions equivalent would require adding a field to frozen gold evidence, which is prohibited and would in any case void the freeze.

Dataset-level: even if the definitions were made identical, NATQ-001 and NATQ-002 are different question sets over the same corpus snapshot with no shared cases. A comparison across them is unpaired and carries no paired statistical interpretation.

The preregistered decision rule does not depend on this. EVAL-NATQ2-H-001 tests SYSTEM-H against the co-run BM25 comparator on the same 40 NATQ-002 cases; the NATQ-001 prior enters only as disclosed context.

h_and_bm25_use_the_same_definition.basis: EVAL-NATQ2-H-001-PREREGISTRATION.json metrics.span_hit is the same predicate the frozen BM25 runner implements, at the same depth, with the same aggregation and denominators. Both score the same 40-case validation partition of NATQ-002.
h_and_bm25_use_the_same_definition.residual_requirement: The SYSTEM-H runner, when written, must implement metrics.span_hit exactly as the BM25 runner does — document identity plus character overlap, no section_path term. A SYSTEM-H runner that reused the NATQ-001 overlaps()/dict_overlaps() helpers would silently score a stricter metric and would not be comparable to the frozen 0.375.
h_and_bm25_use_the_same_definition.recommended_control: The SYSTEM-H runner should recompute the BM25 comparator's case_hit@10 from the frozen ranked output and refuse to proceed unless it reproduces 0.375, proving both systems went through one scorer.
